chapter: Los Angeles: Roy Milton and Central Avenue
title: Back with Roy Milton and young Sonny Criss, Big Jay McNeely
summary: Back at the Cobra Room, and living at the Civic Hotel as teenagers Sonny Criss and Big Jay McNeely listened from the doorway.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: And I came back. And just like Roy said, he got me into the union, and I played at the Cobra Room with them. And it was really nice. He lived down... He had a little grocery store in the next block down the street, and he also worked across the street at the Rendezvous, which was on the northwest corner upstairs -- the Rendezvous, a club up there after-hours. So we were working...
This was also on San Pedro...

Right, San Pedro Street and First; First and San Pedro. And the Downtown House was next to it. And across the street was the Civic Hotel; I lived in the Civic Hotel. And that's when two young saxophone players used to come, and they were too young to come in, they'd come in the back door and stand up against the wall, and listen to me play. It was Big Jay McNeely, the tenor player, and Sonny Criss, the alto saxophone player. They were still in high school, the last year of high school. And later on, Sonny told me that when he heard me, I was the first guy that really had a sound that he really, really admired. He said he looked up there to me, and said, 'That's the way I want to be.' And I was what... I was about twenty at the time. 21. 21 at the time, I think I was. Wait a minute... No, I think I was about two years older... No, I might have been twenty years old at the time. No, 1945, yeah... I hadn't quite made my twenty-first birthday, because that was the beginning of 1945. I wouldn't be 21 until April 26th. Sonny was still in high school; he was about 18 then. So I was a couple of years up on him. And I used to see these two young kids standing there beaming. So they finally got around to introducing themselves, and I invited them to come over to the Civic Hotel some time, and we'd fool around with the horns or whatever.
